title: Forms VII (infaʿala) & VIII (iftaʿala)
source: Original instructional lesson authored for this application (syllabus ref: Haywood & Nahmad Ch. 22; Ryding Ch. 28–29)
objectives: Recognize Form VII (اِنْفَعَلَ) as an intrinsic passive / unaccusative stem.
Recognize Form VIII (اِفْتَعَلَ) by its infixed ـتَـ after the first radical.
Recover underlying roots from Form VIII dental/emphatic/wāw assimilations (e.g., اِتَّحَدَ from و-ح-د).
recallPrompt: From Chapter 21: Which vowel marks the imperfect prefix of Forms V and VI?

sections.heading: Prefix اِنْـ (VII) and Infix ـتَـ (VIII)
sections.body: Form VII (اِنْفَعَلَ) prefixes نْـ (with hamzat al-waṣl) and is always intransitive/medio-passive ('to become broken, opened'). Form VIII (اِفْتَعَلَ) infixes ـتَـ directly after the first radical and often expresses reflexive participation or personal effort.

sections.label: Form VIII Phonotactic Assimilation
sections.summary: In Form VIII, infixed ـتَـ changes when C1 is: (1) و/ي → assimilates to تّ (و-ح-د → اِتَّحَدَ); (2) د/ذ/ز → becomes د (ذ-ك-ر → اِذَّكَرَ / ز-ح-م → اِزْدَحَمَ); (3) ص/ض/ط/ظ → becomes emphatic ط (ص-ب-ر → اِصْطَبَرَ).

sections.heading: Form VII & Form VIII Assimilation Examples
rows: Infixed ت becomes ط after ص

sections.translation: The students gathered in the hall.
sections.irab: اِجْتَمَعَ: فِعْلٌ مَاضٍ (وَزْنُ اِفْتَعَلَ، جَذْرُ ج-م-ع) | الطُّلَّابُ: فَاعِلٌ مَرْفُوعٌ
sections.notes: Strip the initial hamzat al-waṣl (اِ) and the infixed ـتَـ to isolate the triliteral root ج-م-ع.

sections.heading: Dictionary Lookup Trap
sections.body: Never look up اِتَّقَى or اِتَّحَدَ under the letter ت! Doubled تّ at the start of a Form VIII verb almost always hides an initial و (و-ق-ي, و-ح-د).
